abstract_evidence_excerpt: Alternating wetting and drying cycles in paddy soils drive active biogeochemical processes and profoundly influence pollutant migration and transformation. The results demonstrate that ROS generation primarily arises from microbially mediated Fe-(II) accumulation during flooding, followed by Fenton-like oxidation upon reoxygenation.
